skill.name: compress
skill.description: Compress natural language memory files such as CLAUDE.md, todos, and preferences into a shorter caveman format. The skill preserves technical details, code blocks, URLs, paths, commands, and markdown structure. It writes a backup before replacing the original file.
skill.summary: Compress markdown and text memory files while preserving technical details and structure.
skill.author: juliusbrussee

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from markdown examples, regex patterns, and an explicit denylist for sensitive files. The main residual risks are intentional submission of selected file contents to Claude and LLM-mediated overwrites of local files. The subprocess call uses fixed arguments, and obvious credential paths are refused before file reads.

remediation.issue: Selected file contents are sent to Claude through the Anthropic API or local Claude CLI.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before each remote compression and describe the third-party data boundary in the CLI output.

remediation.issue: The tool accepts any resolvable file path that passes heuristic checks.
remediation.suggestion: Add an optional workspace allowlist or require paths under the current project unless the user explicitly overrides it.

remediation.issue: Raw file content is embedded in an LLM prompt before the result overwrites the original file.
remediation.suggestion: Show a diff before overwrite or require confirmation when validation warnings remain after compression.

remediation.issue: The Claude CLI fallback executes an external binary from the local environment.
remediation.suggestion: Make the CLI fallback opt-in or document how the executable is resolved before it receives file content.

semantic_findings.title: Third-party API submission of selected file contents
semantic_findings.description: The skill reads the selected file and sends its full text to Claude through the Anthropic SDK or Claude CLI. This is disclosed and partly guarded by sensitive-path checks, but it crosses a third-party data boundary.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The implementation directly reads original_text and passes a prompt containing it to the Anthropic client or Claude CLI. The skill instructions also state that Claude is called to compress.

semantic_findings.title: LLM-controlled output overwrites the original file
semantic_findings.description: The compression prompt embeds raw file content and writes the model output back to the original path after creating a backup. Validation checks structure, URLs, and code blocks, but malicious prose in the source file could still influence the rewrite.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The prompt includes untrusted file text and the resulting LLM output is written to disk. Backups and validation reduce impact, but they do not fully prevent prompt-influenced content changes.

content.value_statement: Long memory files consume context tokens and slow agent sessions. This skill compresses prose while preserving headings, URLs, code blocks, paths, and commands.
actual_capabilities: Detects natural language markdown and text files before compression.
Skips common code and configuration file extensions.
Sends selected file text to Claude through the Anthropic API or Claude CLI.
Preserves markdown headings, URLs, code blocks, inline code, paths, and commands.
Creates an original-file backup before writing compressed content.
Validates output and retries targeted fixes when preservation checks fail.
limitations: It is intended only for markdown and text natural language files.
It sends selected file contents to Claude, so confidential content needs review.
Sensitive-file detection is heuristic and can miss unusual secret names.
Compression quality depends on the model response and validation coverage.

use_cases.title: Reduce project memory size
use_cases.description: Compress a long CLAUDE.md or agent memory file while keeping technical details intact.

use_cases.title: Prepare concise team notes
use_cases.description: Shorten markdown todo lists or preference files before sharing them across agent sessions.

use_cases.title: Audit preserved technical content
use_cases.description: Use the backup and validation checks to compare compressed notes with the original source.

prompt_templates.title: Compress one memory file
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single known file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compress my project memory file at /absolute/path/to/CLAUDE.md.

prompt_templates.title: Compress notes with preservation focus
prompt_templates.scenario: User wants a shorter file but must keep technical references unchanged.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compress /absolute/path/to/notes.md and preserve all URLs, commands, file paths, and code blocks.

prompt_templates.title: Check whether a file is suitable
prompt_templates.scenario: User is unsure whether the target is natural language or config.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect /absolute/path/to/project-memory.txt and compress it only if it is safe natural language content.

prompt_templates.title: Compress and review preservation warnings
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for sensitive documentation changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compress /absolute/path/to/team-preferences.md, then report any validation warnings and the backup file location.

output_examples.input: A long CLAUDE.md file with repeated workflow reminders, commands, URLs, and markdown headings.
output_examples.output: A shorter markdown memory file that keeps headings, URLs, commands, paths, and code blocks unchanged.

output_examples.input: A prose todo file with duplicate planning notes and several technical references.
output_examples.output: A compact todo file with redundant phrasing removed and technical references preserved.

output_examples.input: A markdown preference file that already has a matching backup file beside it.
output_examples.output: A refusal message that avoids overwriting the existing backup and leaves the original file unchanged.

best_practices: Review the target file for confidential content before running compression.
Keep the generated backup until you verify the compressed file.
Use absolute paths so the CLI compresses the intended file.
anti_patterns: Do not compress secrets, credentials, private keys, or sensitive environment files.
Do not use this skill for source code, configuration files, or lock files.
Do not delete the backup before checking validation warnings and important content.

faq.question: What files can this skill compress?
faq.answer: It targets markdown, text, and similar natural language memory files. It skips many code and configuration extensions.

faq.question: Does it keep code blocks unchanged?
faq.answer: It instructs Claude to preserve code blocks and validates that fenced code blocks match the original.

faq.question: What happens to the original file?
faq.answer: The skill creates a backup named after the original file before writing the compressed version.

faq.question: Does it send my file to a remote service?
faq.answer: Yes. It sends selected file contents to Claude through the Anthropic API or Claude CLI.

faq.question: Can it compress files that contain secrets?
faq.answer: It tries to refuse obvious secret files, but you should review content before use.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
